context: Hegel's Geist is mind understood not as a private consciousness but as a shared, historical reality: the customs, institutions, art, religion and philosophy through which a people understands itself. The Phenomenology of Spirit traces its development to self-knowing 'absolute spirit'.

context: The characteristic outlook of an age. Herder and others popularised the idea; Hegel held that philosophy is its own time comprehended in thought, so no thinker can leap beyond his age.

context: For Hegel, history is the progress of the consciousness of freedom, carried by a world spirit working through nations and individuals. Watching Napoleon ride through Jena in 1806, he wrote of seeing 'the world soul on horseback'.

quote.translation: This character of Dasein's being, veiled in its whence and whither but disclosed all the more unveiledly in itself, this 'that it is', we call the thrownness of this entity into its 'there'.

quote.text: 是以聖人處無為之事，行不言之教
quote.translation: Therefore the sage dwells in the affairs of non-action and practises the teaching without words.

image.credit: Zhang Lu · Public domain · via Wikimedia Commons

context: The central Confucian virtue: the fully human goodness shown in care for others, rooted in family affection and refined through ritual. The character combines 'person' and 'two', suggesting that one is human in relationship.
attribution_note: Quote checked verbatim against Chinese Wikisource

quote.text: 孝弟也者，其爲仁之本與？
quote.translation: Filial piety and brotherly respect: are they not the root of humaneness?

image.credit: Anonymous Chinese painter of the Western Han period · Public domain · via Wikimedia Commons

context: Li covers ceremony, etiquette and the whole web of proper social forms. For Confucius ritual is not empty formality: practised with sincerity, it shapes character and makes harmony between people possible.
attribution_note: Quote checked verbatim against Chinese Wikisource

quote.text: 克己復禮爲仁
quote.translation: To master oneself and return to ritual propriety is humaneness.

image.credit: Anonymous Chinese painter of the Western Han period · Public domain · via Wikimedia Commons

translation: that which upholds; duty, law, teaching
context: In Hindu thought dharma is the cosmic and moral order and each person's duty within it; in the Bhagavad Gita, Arjuna must do his duty as a warrior. In Buddhism it names the Buddha's teaching and also the basic constituents of experience.
attribution_note: Quote checked verbatim against GRETIL (Göttingen Register of Electronic Texts in Indian Languages)

quote.text: śreyān sva-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt svanuṣṭhitāt
quote.translation: Better one's own dharma done imperfectly than another's dharma done well.

image.alt: Krishna and Arjuna on the chariot (Indian painting, 18th–19th c.)
image.credit: Unknown artist · Public domain · via Wikimedia Commons

context: For the Buddhist philosopher Nāgārjuna, all things are empty of svabhāva, intrinsic self-existence: they arise only in dependence on causes and concepts. Emptiness itself is empty, so it is not a hidden absolute but the end of all fixed views.
attribution_note: Quote checked verbatim against GRETIL

quote.text: yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ śūnyatāṃ tāṃ pracakṣmahe
quote.translation: Whatever is dependent arising, that we call emptiness.

image.credit: Unknown | Recovered from Himalayan Art Resources · Public domain · via Wikimedia Commons

context: The Upanishads teach that the innermost self, ātman, is identical with brahman, the ground of all reality: 'tat tvam asi', you are that. The Buddha denied any such permanent self (anātman), and the dispute shaped Indian philosophy for centuries.
attribution_note: Quote checked verbatim against GRETIL

quote.text: tat satyam | sa ātmā | tat tvam asi śvetaketo
quote.translation: That is the real. That is the self. You are that, Śvetaketu.

image.credit: Raja Ravi Varma · Public domain · via Wikimedia Commons

context: Avicenna distinguished what a thing is (māhiyya) from the fact that it exists (wujūd). In all created things existence is added to essence; only in the Necessary Existent are they one. Through Latin translations this shaped Aquinas and the whole scholastic debate.
attribution_note: Quote checked verbatim against OpenITI corpus (0428IbnSina.ShifaIlahiyyat)

quote.text: فإن لكل أمر حقيقة هو بها ما هو، فالمثلث حقيقة أنه مثلث، وللبياض حقيقة أنه بياض، وذلك هو الذي ربما سميناه الوجود الخاص
quote.translation: For each thing has a reality by which it is what it is: the triangle has the reality of being a triangle, whiteness the reality of being whiteness; and this is what we have perhaps called its proper existence.

image.credit: National Library of Medicine · Public domain · via Wikimedia Commons

context: Falsafa names the tradition of Arabic philosophy that absorbed Aristotle and Neoplatonism: al-Kindī, al-Fārābī, Avicenna, Averroes. Averroes' commentaries were so influential in Latin Europe that he was simply called 'the Commentator'.
attribution_note: Quote checked verbatim against OpenITI corpus (0595IbnRushdHafid.FaslMaqal)

quote.text: أن نفحص، على جهة النظر الشرعي، هل النظر في الفلسفة وعلوم المنطق مباح بالشرع، أم محظور، أم مأمور به
quote.translation: [The aim of this treatise is] to examine, from the standpoint of religious law, whether the study of philosophy and the sciences of logic is permitted by the Law, forbidden, or commanded.
